hook: A U.S. Air Force ISR platform from the 124th Attack Squadron observed a single UAP traveling northwest at low altitude over the Gulf of Aden on July 14, 2024, during a routine target development mission in the USCENTCOM area of responsibility. The standardized MISREP captures the UAP's observed flight characteristics, coordinates, and the observer's formal assessments across a structured set of data fields.
why_it_matters: This report documents an incidental UAP encounter during an active intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance mission supporting both NAVCENT and AFCENT, indicating the object appeared in a militarily active operational theater. The formal MISREP structure and its routing through USCENTCOM to AARO demonstrates the post-NDAA UAP reporting pipeline functioning as intended for theater-level incidents. The observer's assessment of 'benign' combined with UNKNOWN determinations across propulsion, intelligent control, and advanced capabilities illustrates the limits of characterization from a single airborne sensor platform.

key_findings.finding: The UAP was observed flying a straight, level trajectory to the northwest at low altitude, and its speed exceeded that of the observing aircraft, which pursued it until the distance became prohibitive.

quotes.text: UAP MANEUVERABILITY OBSERVATIONS: STRAIGHT FLIGHT PATH AT SAME ALTI
UAP'S SPEED WAS FASTER THAN THE 1.4a, 1.4g FLYING SPEED
FOLLOWED THE UAP TILL THE DISTANCE BECAME TOO FAR TO FOLLOW

key_findings.finding: The UAP was tracked from a first observed position to a last observed position along a northwest trajectory at an estimated low kinetic altitude, with a 5-unit radius uncertainty on both positional fixes.

The observer made no attempt to interrogate or engage the UAP, and formal assessments recorded propulsion means, intelligent control, and advanced capabilities all as UNKNOWN, with no effects on persons or equipment and no material recovery.

quotes.text: Observation Interrogation of UAP (yes/no; if yes list sensor(s) and returns):: NO
UAP Under Intelligent Control (yes/no; if yes, describe): UNKNOWN
UAP Advanced Capabilities And/Or Materials  (yes/no; if yes, describe): UNKNOWN ABOUT ADVANCED CAPABILITIES AND/OR MATERIALS

key_findings.finding: The UAP encounter was incidental to an ongoing target development ISR mission; the observing Air Force asset from the 124th Attack Squadron was supporting NAVCENT when the sighting occurred, and resumed separate AFCENT tasking afterward.

quotes.text: 1.4a OBSERVED 1X UAP AT 140517ZJUL24 IVO 38P MT 53 1.4a 17 1.4a (SEE UAP1).  FROM 141041ZJUL24 TO 142130ZJUL24, 1.4a CONDUCTED TARGET DEVELOPMENT ISO AFCENT IVO 38P MV 24 1.4a 81 1.4a (SEE ISR 2).

key_findings.finding: The observer formally assessed the UAP as benign, and the report was classified SECRET/REL TO USA, FVEY before being approved for release to AARO by the USCENTCOM Chief of Staff on June 2, 2025, nearly a year after the incident.

legacy_program_connections.reasoning: The document is explicitly stamped 'Approved for Release to AARO' and was processed through USCENTCOM's mandatory declassification review (MDR 25-0072) specifically for AARO disclosure.
The document carries a REL TO USA, FVEY caveat throughout, indicating the UAP report was shared or sharable with the Five Eyes intelligence alliance partners.
